feature: Marketing Free Scan page (/scan) — the real consent gate (Git #1361): the start form captures name/company/work email and its POST /api/public/free-scan/start fires the real lead + returns the read app's real scopes; 'Review access and continue' advances to the new consent-disclosure screen (scopes card generated from REQUIRED_MT_SCOPES + the 'Not requested' counter-list) rather than straight to scanning.
notes: Git #1361 replaced the single-checkbox Free Scan → Scan flow with a real consent gate:
start → consent → granting → scanning → results. Only the start form and the new consent/
granting screens changed; the scanning + results phases are still the SIMULATED fixture from
the Part 2 rebuild (Design/free-scan-consent-export/Marketing Free Scan.dc.html).
SCOPE OF THIS MANIFEST — what is deterministically assertable:
1. POST /api/public/free-scan/start (apiTests): rejects an invalid email 400 (no lead fired),
and for a valid payload returns { ok: true, scopes: [...] } where scopes is the read app's
REAL REQUIRED_MT_SCOPES (asserted by the presence of Directory.Read.All / AuditLog.Read.All).
This proves the consent screen's scopes list is generated from the manifest, not hand-typed.
Accepted side effect (same class as read-consent-flow.json): the valid call stages one real
funnel lead for the testbed email via ensureLeadForEmail (source 'assessment'), idempotent.
2. GET /scan mounts the real page (data-testid=freescan-page), the start phase renders its final
hero copy and the NEW lead-capture controls (name / company / work-email inputs + the
'Review access and continue' button).
3. Filling name/company/email, ticking consent, and clicking the button advances to the consent
DISCLOSURE screen (data-testid=freescan-consent-screen) with its real H1 ('This scan needs
read access...'), at least one real read scope (Directory.Read.All) in the scopes card, the
'Not requested' counter-list, and the 'Grant read-only access' button — proving the new
consent phase is inserted and rendered.
DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, documented honestly rather than faked:
- The 'Grant read-only access' click is NOT exercised: it opens Microsoft's own admin-consent
screen in a popup (real OAuth) and mints a real checkout session — the OAuth wall is
architecturally undrivable by this harness (same caveat read-consent-flow.json carries). The
granting → scanning resume-on-callback is covered by that real mechanism, not a mock.
- The six-sector scanner animation and the results screen: still SIMULATED on timers (no Graph
call), ~9.6s of stepped animation, and every number is authored demo data — not a stable or
meaningful assertion target.
DEPLOYED-ORIGIN CAVEAT (same class the sibling marketing manifests carry): asserts against
{{DEPLOY_URL}}, which reflects the new endpoint + this page only once the marketing site and
api-server are redeployed. Until then, /api/public/free-scan/start 404s and /scan may resolve to
the old flow — failures on that ground are deployment lag, not a page defect. The consent-screen
UI steps are robust to the endpoint being absent: if the scopes fetch fails, the card falls back
to the curated (manifest-verified) scope list, so Directory.Read.All still renders.
